plan_a_advantages: Includes hill repeats, which are essential for building the strength and power needed for climbing on trails.
Incorporates interval training to improve speed and running economy.
Higher overall volume allows for greater physiological adaptation and potential for improvement.
More varied workout types provide a more well-rounded training stimulus.
plan_b_advantages: Lower overall volume may be beneficial for athletes prone to injury or those new to trail running.
Emphasis on easy aerobic work builds a strong base without excessive fatigue.
The strength and mobility session is a valuable addition for injury prevention and overall athleticism.
reasoning: Given the goal of becoming a faster trail runner, Plan A appears to be the better choice. While both plans incorporate essential elements like rest and long runs, Plan A includes a more diverse range of workouts specifically geared towards speed and strength development crucial for trail running. The inclusion of hill repeats and interval training in Plan A directly addresses the demands of trail terrain, whereas Plan B focuses more on consistent, easy aerobic work and a single tempo run. The higher volume in Plan A, while requiring more recovery, also provides more opportunity for adaptation and improvement.
